newsitem.title: USA: Craig, Colo. 408 MW coal-fired unit seen up Thurs.
newsitem.headline: Craig, Colo. 408 MW coal-fired unit seen up Thurs.

text.p: The 408 megawatt (MW) unit 3 at the Craig coal-fired power plant in Colorado will begin restart Tuesday night but is unlikely to generate power until late Thursday, a spokesman for the Tri-State Generation and Transmission Association said Tuesday.
The unit was shut early this month for planned maintenance.

The spokesman said testing will be conducted on the unit after boilers are refired late Tuesday, and the unit will likely remain at half capacity for 12 hours or so after being cleared for full operation.
The plant also has two 428 MW units, which continued to operate at full capacity.
In addition to Tri-State, owners of the Craig station are Public Service Co of Colorado, PacifiCorp, the Salt River Project and the Platte River Authority.
